outcome: Placental morphology (fetal capillary branching, maternal blood spaces, external trophectoderm cell number)
cohort: Pregnant rats, with one group exposed to intermittent hypoxia and a control group.
finding: Gestational intermittent hypoxia (GIH) exposure in pregnant rats resulted in no significant differences in maternal or fetal weight at birth, but GIH male offspring had significantly lower weight at 14 days, and their placentas showed increased fetal capillary branching, expanded maternal blood spaces, increased number of external trophectoderm cells, and enlargement in experimental males.
followup_time: Up to 14 days post-birth for offspring weight; measurements also taken one day before delivery date.
birth_weight: Fetal weight was measured at the end of gestation, showing no significant differences between groups.
gest_age: Exposure occurred during the last 2 weeks of gestation; some measurements were taken one day before the delivery date, and some offspring were allowed to be born at term.
